questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Mandatory stay

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not choose Taiwan, it was a mandatory stay

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult, there was loads of miscommunication between KU and NTNU. The teachers had very different expectations for us based on what KU told them, which made the entire process very mentally taxing because we weren't prepared.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None really, we had to pressure KU to set up a zoom meeting so we could air out all of our concerns, one of them being the lack of help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: KU gave us false information that we had to get our hands on a health statement. This was extremely constly and time consuming, as we had to schedule doctors appointments and get unneccesary X-rays done. We only found out at the visa office that it was not neccessary.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult, a lot of trial and error. We stayed at an airbnb for the first month while we searched for something more permanent. I lived in a 5 room apartment with no kitchen which i shared with 4 other girls, for about 3500kr per month. I knew some found their own apartments, some had to share.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Do not sign a contract unless it's in english, or you're well spoken enough in mandarin to understand. Our landlady specifically rented out to foreigners so she spoke english well. Do not fret if you find a perfect place and it's a bit further away from university, I walked every single day for about 20 minutes and it was honestly not so bad. The public transport is amazing in Taiwan, everything is connected if you need to go somewhere.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no university housing offered to foreigners, we had to find something ourselves.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We were automatically enrolled in courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were automatically enrolled so there was no need for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We did not have a choice in the classes that we took.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There really isn't any when it comes to mandatory stays.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The levels were okay, not any more challenging than back home, except for the amount of mandatory homework assigned every single day, which was quite overwhelming.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There really wasn't any understanding for bad days, you were expected to perform every single day like your life depended on it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: It was intensive Chinese language course.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Intensive will get you good very quickly because you're forced to speak in class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None really, our phone bill was paid in full, so that was quite expensive one time payment, but besides that not really.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The food and drinks are ridiculously cheap in Taiwan. We had food delivery every single day due to the lack of kitchen and it was super cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a couple of clubs, but majority tailored to local students and some had even refused to take in a foreigner. They're conducted in Chinese so if you don't speak it, you wouldn't be able to participate.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: See other places in Taiwan, Taichung is lively and the people are kind, the same can be said for Tainan. Tainan is amazing if you're a history nerd, it had so many beautiful spots. Its easy getting high speed rail tickets to go someplace else, visit some of the small isles as well for beautiful beaches.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and see some museums in Taipei, visit historical sites in Tainan, go and shop in Taichung. Go to Shilin night market, it has everything you need. My favorite place in Taipei was Ximen, best place to buy kpop albums, and anime merch. Go and experience a traditional tea ceremony as well, it's worth it. The Taipei zoo is massive as well and you can spend an entire day in there.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Initially hard because of the lack of english proficiency among the locals, i was forced to speak Chinese which worked out for the best in the end.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didn't have any communication with local students as my university department was strictly for foreigners coming to learn Chinese.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Getting used to the garbage trucks blasting the same song over and over again is something you'll have to do. The busses also have no regard for your wellbeing, so expect to be thrown around and pretend as if you're in a fast & furious franchise. It's a cash based society, so you have to get comfortable with planning a budget and paying cash everywhere you go.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are genuinely kind when they hear your feeble attempts to communicate in Chinese, they appreciate it, so don't be scared. They're also very polite, people move quickly because Taipei is a big city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do not take everything the teachers say to heart. Sometimes they can say genuinely mean spirited things (flashbacks to my teacher telling me that i didn't deserve to be there) just treat them as a military recruiter. 
2. Wave down the busses when you want them stop for you, otherwise they won't. 
3. Please bring a jacket, once the weather cools down you will be freezing, even though it's technically 15 degrees which would be tshirt weather for us. We adapt to the temperature.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to conversate in Chinese with my uber driver on my way to the airport, i wasn't even nervous. Oh and also being able to speak in Chinese on the phone to my delivery drivers, that was a big pat on the back moment for me.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being homesick, living in a room without a window (please don't make the same mistake thinking it'll be okay, i promise sunlight does so much for us).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
